column1: title: Cautious magma approach (warm and damp dig markers)
tags: dig, marker, warm dig, damp dig, magma, aquifer, safety
description: A branching approach tunnel that demonstrates the dig markers
column2: the safety prefixes no earlier example touched. A marker is one or more letters written in front of a dig symbol (the doc gives the stacked example mwmdd). The three markers are mw (warm dig)
column4: and mb (marker or "blueprint" mode). Here the center shaft is plain d
column5: ordinary rock a miner digs without pause. The west gallery is mwd: warm dig marks tiles next to magma or warm stone
column6: so the miner stops and asks before breaching them instead of tapping straight into a magma sea and burning. The east gallery is mdd: damp dig marks tiles next to water or an aquifer
column7: so the miner pauses instead of flooding the fort. The junction tile mwmdd stacks both markers (warm and damp at once)
column8: exactly the form the reference lists. The tile below the junction is mbd: marker mode places the designation but leaves it held
column9: so miners ignore it until you convert it to a live dig in game (handy for staging a dig you want to release later
column10: on your signal). Marker order does not matter and any marker can carry a priority or an extent too (for example mwd3 or mwmdd(10x10)). These markers change nothing about the shape you dig
column11: only how cautiously the miners approach it
column12: so use them on any tunnel that runs toward magma
